tone_statements.citation: MERN (Mission évangélique réformée néerlandaise). 2020-2024. Alfabɛti Mɔgɔfin (Mogofin alphabet page) and site 'amarenkama.com' (language pages, numerals, proverbs, tales).
tone_statements.quote: Le ton — En Mogofin, dans certains cas, un mot ou une phrase peut avoir deux sens qui sont distingués seulement par leur ton. báa (la chèvre) baa (la trace); fuga (les cheveux blancs) fuga (la brousse); kɔtɛ (tout de suite) kɔtɛ (ancien, vieux); sori (porter) sori (puiser); lɔ́gɛ́ (le jour) lɔgɛ (l’arbre); tárán (prier) taran (trouver)
tone_statements.translation: Tone — In Mogofin, in certain cases, a word or a phrase can have two meanings that are distinguished only by their tone. báa 'goat' vs baa 'track'; fuga 'white hair' vs fuga 'bush'; kɔtɛ 'right away' vs kɔtɛ 'old'; sori 'carry' vs sori 'draw water'; lɔ́gɛ́ 'day' vs lɔgɛ 'tree'; tárán 'pray' vs taran 'find'.
tone_statements.locator: web page 'Langue mogofin', section 'Divers' > 'Le ton' (after 'La consonne à la fin des mots', before 'Les mots "empruntés"')
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

tone_statements.citation: Выдрин, В. Ф. 2003. Тональные системы языков манде: краткий обзор [Tonal systems of Mande languages: a short survey]. Вопросы языкознания 2003, № 2: 95–113.
tone_statements.quote: В подгруппе моколе сравнительно хорошо описан только один язык, коранко [Kastenholz 1987]. Его тональная система достаточно близка к прототипу манден. Судя по моим полевым материалам по трем другим языкам подгруппы, то же можно сказать и о них. [p. 97:] ...достаточно гомогенная глубинная структура, которую, очевидно, следует отнести и к уровню праманден: два тональных уровня, downstep и downdrift, две тонемы, В и Н-В.
tone_statements.translation: In the Mokole subgroup only one language, Koranko, is comparatively well described [Kastenholz 1987]. Its tonal system is fairly close to the Manding prototype. Judging by my field materials on the three other languages of the subgroup, the same can be said of them. [p. 97:] ...a fairly homogeneous deep structure, which evidently should also be attributed to the Proto-Manding level: two tonal levels, downstep and downdrift, two tonemes, H and L-H.
tone_statements.locator: p. 98, last paragraph of section '1. Манден' (immediately before '2.1. Сосо (сусу)'); prototype definition p. 97, first paragraph of '1. Манден'; Schema 1 (family tree with Mokole members) p. 111

sources.note: Not about Mogofin: §4.1.2.1 (par. 62) 'There are four languages in the Mokole group: Kakabé, Kuranko, Lélé, and Mogofin.. little published data is available for Mogofin'; Kuranko (Kastenholz 1987) used as the Mokole exemplar. sources.citation: Vydrine, Valentin. 2009. Esquisse de la langue lélé (groupe mokolé). Mandenkan 45: 29-104.
sources.note: About Lele, not Mogofin; group-level remark only: §3.3 (p. 42) 'Le système tonal lélé est typique des langues mandé et mokolé : deux registres; la déclinaison tonale (down-drift); deux classes tonales principales de mots.' Mogofin appears only in the lexicostatistical table (§2) and in the remark that Mogofin and Kakabe are phonologically and morphologically very close.

sources.citation: Vydrina, Alexandra & Valentin Vydrin. 2022. The Kakabe dialectal continuum: A lexicostatistical study. Language in Africa 3(1): 31-56. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2022-3-1-31-56
sources.note: Nothing on stress. English version of the 2014 study; p. 35: 'The Mogofin data, given for external comparison, are drawn from (Polinder et al. 2009), and some missing terms were supplied by our field data' — the Mogofin column carries tone marks throughout; no prose on Mogofin prosody.

tone.translation: Tone — In Mogofin, in certain cases, a word or a phrase can have two meanings that are distinguished only by their tone. báa 'goat' vs baa 'track'; fuga 'white hair' vs fuga 'bush'; kɔtɛ 'right away' vs kɔtɛ 'old'; sori 'carry' vs sori 'draw water'; lɔ́gɛ́ 'day' vs lɔgɛ 'tree'; tárán 'pray' vs taran 'find'.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.says: States that in Mogofin a word or phrase can have two meanings distinguished only by tone, and gives six minimal pairs, the high-toned member written with acute accents in three of them (báa 'chèvre' vs baa 'trace'; lɔ́gɛ́ 'jour' vs lɔgɛ 'arbre'; tárán 'prier' vs taran 'trouver'; fuga/fuga, kɔtɛ/kɔtɛ, sori/sori printed without diacritics). No count of tones, no statement on stress; the practical orthography otherwise leaves tone unmarked.

Langue mogofin / La langue Mogofin [orthography guide page: L'alphabet, consonnes spécifiques, phonèmes composés, consonne finale, 'Divers: Le ton', mots empruntés]. amarenkama.com (Mogofin / Mikhifore / Mixifore website), French and English versions.

sources.citation: Vydrina, Alexandra. 2017. A corpus-based description of Kakabe, a Western Mande language: prosody in grammar. PhD thesis, INALCO (HAL tel-03203594).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on Mogofin stress or tone. Mogofin is mentioned only as Kakabe's closest relative (p. 40: 'Kakabe and Mogofin are mutually-intellegible') and in the literature survey (p. 45: 'a M.A. thesis by Jacqueline Janse on Mogofin in Dutch (1999a) published also as a grammar sketch in French (Janse 1999b)'). Phonology chapters concern Kakabe only.

sources.citation: Vydrina, Alexandra & Valentin Vydrin. 2014. Предварительные наброски к диалектологии какабе [Preliminary sketches of Kakabe dialectology], pp. 229-251 (HAL halshs-00961389).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Table 1 gives a 100-item Swadesh list for Mogofin (from the authors' field notes and the MERN 'Lexique mɔgɔfin 2009') with lexical H/L tone marks on every word (e.g. bɛ́ɛ 'all', bùgùtá 'ashes', kóndéŋ-è 'bird'); p. 241 says the Mogofin data come from their own field records and the Lexique.

sources.citation: Polinder, Wim, Jacqueline Janse & Kees Jan van Linden. 2009-. Lexique / Dictionnaire Mɔgɔfin-Français. Garama (Boké): Mission Évangélique Réformée Néerlandaise — online Dictionary-App-Builder version, letters A and B.
sources.note: No front matter, no prose on tone or stress. Entries carry a per-syllable tone string in slash notation (e.g. 'abada / / / adv jamais', 'adamadeŋɛ / \ \ / \ n homme', 'aligiyama \ \ \ / / n au-delà', 'ale \ \ PrPers lui'), i.e. the compilers treat Mogofin as a two-tone (H/L) language with lexically specified tone on every syllable.

sources.citation: Vydrine, Valentin. 1998. Sur l'écriture mandingue et mandé en caractères arabes (mandinka, bambara, soussou, mogofin). Mandenkan 33, 87 pp. Section 6 'L'adjami mogofin' (printed pp. 19-21) + 'Textes mogofin' (Texte 14, Alhousseyni Diallo).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sections 6.1-6.3 describe how consonants, vowels (a i u e/ɛ o/ɔ), vowel length and nasalisation are rendered in the Mogofin Arabic-script texts; the Mogofin texts are transcribed with tone marks, and fn. 55 says the tone/length notation is only preliminary. Vydrine also says a 'description préliminaire du mogofin' (with Mamadi Diane, IRLA Conakry, fieldwork April 1996) 'sera publiée prochainement'.

sources.citation: Выдрин, Валентин Феодосьевич. 2006. К реконструкции фонологического типа и именной морфологии пра-манде [Towards a reconstruction of the phonological type and nominal morphology of Proto-Mande]. Acta Linguistica Petropolitana. Труды Института лингвистических исследований, т. II, ч. 2. Санкт-Петербург.
sources.note: No description of the Mogofin tone system; the Mokole source survey states that the two small missionary grammars of Mogofin (Janse 1998, Janse 1999) do not take tones into account and that the author has his own field materials; section 2 'phonological type of Proto-Mande' covers mono- vs disyllabism, vowel systems and consonant harmony (no per-language tone section); Mogofin words are cited with tone marks in the comparative data. Useful as a documented statement that the known Janse grammars will NOT yield a tone description.

tone.quote: Только коранко описан сравнительно хорошо: имеется грамматика и небольшой словарь [Kastenholz 1987а; Kastenholz 1987b]. По леле и какабе я располагаю только собственными полевыми материалами. По могофин имеются две небольшие миссионерские грамматики, не учитывающие тонов [Janse 1998, Janse 1999], а также мои полевые материалы.
tone.locator: §1.1.1.2 'Моколе' (pp. 22-24 per the article's TOC), last paragraph of the subsection
tone.translation: Only Koranko is described comparatively well: there is a grammar and a small dictionary [Kastenholz 1987a; 1987b]. For Lele and Kakabe I have only my own field materials. For Mogofin there are two small missionary grammars which do not take tones into account [Janse 1998, Janse 1999], as well as my field materials.
